name: Do I need an architect or engineer to design my tiny home plans for permitting?

mainEntity.name: Do I need an architect or engineer to design my tiny home plans for permitting?

acceptedAnswer.text: For permitting a tiny home, particularly if it's considered a permanent structure or an ADU, you will often need plans stamped by a licensed architect or engineer. This ensures the structural integrity, safety, and code compliance of the design, which is a requirement for most building departments. While some very simple structures or manufactured homes may have pre-approved plans, custom tiny homes or those requiring specific foundation work typically necessitate professional architectural and engineering input. This expertise helps navigate complex building codes and streamlines the permit application process, reducing potential delays or rejections.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, for permitting a permanent tiny home or ADU, plans often need to be stamped by a licensed architect or engineer to ensure structural integrity, safety, and code compliance.
